chunks: Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the days of sacrifice in Mina. He said: “Four days.”
And about the sacrifice in the rest of the towns, he said: “Three days.”
And he said: “If a man arrives to his family two days after al-Adha, he may perform the sacrifice on the third day in which he arrives.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَيَّامٍ: four days, the period for sacrifice in Mina
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: the sacrifice of Eid al-Adha, or the days associated with it in this context
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Mina, the sacred location near Mecca where hajj rites are performed
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: three days, the period for sacrifice outside Mina
key_terms.سَائِرِ الْبُلْدَانِ: the rest of the towns or regions outside Mina

ai.seo_question: How many days is the Eid al-Adha sacrifice valid in Mina and in other towns?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal time frame for offering the sacrifice of Eid al-Adha: four days in Mina and three days in other towns. It also clarifies that if a man returns to his family two days after al-Adha, he may still offer the sacrifice on the third day upon his arrival.
